title: Catalog
description: Every list of kinds in the game. Kinds are data: code reads their properties, never their names.

sailors.description: The figures that sail the boats. The first is the one drawn until players choose their own.

regimes.description: The kinds of spell of weather.

WeatherSea.title: WeatherSea
WeatherSea.description: The waves long enough to move a boat: the band of wavelengths they span and the spectrum that gives each its height.

sigmaBelow.description: The peak's width below the peak frequency.

sigmaAbove.description: The peak's width above the peak frequency.

spreading.description: The directional spreading's exponent s in cos²ˢ(θ/2): a whole number.

fetchCap.description: The fetch of open water, in nautical miles.

cull.description: Waves lower than this fraction of an area's highest are left out.

WeatherDisk.title: WeatherDisk
WeatherDisk.description: The wind over the disk: how its speed rises toward the rim, the refuge at the centre, the stronger gusts of the outer waters and the turning of the difference across the disk.

speedCentre.description: The wind's speed at the centre, as a share of a spell's wind at mid-disk.

speedRim.description: The wind's speed at the rim, as a share of a spell's wind at mid-disk.

rim.description: Where the speed reaches its share at the rim: the mist band, in nautical miles.

refugeInner.description: Within this the refuge's limits hold in full, in nautical miles.

refugeOuter.description: Beyond this the refuge's limits do not hold, in nautical miles.

refugeMeanKnee.description: The refuge softens the mean wind above this, in knots.

refugeMean.description: The mean wind the refuge holds to, in knots.

refugeWindKnee.description: The refuge softens the wind with its gusts above this, in knots.

refugeWind.description: The wind with its gusts the refuge holds to, in knots.

rimGusts.description: The gust factor's excess over 1 grows by this share toward the rim.

rimGustsFrom.description: From here to the rim, in nautical miles.

acrossTurn.description: The shortest and longest time the axis of the wind's difference across the disk takes to turn once, in hours.

WeatherGusts.title: WeatherGusts
WeatherGusts.description: The gust field: gradient noise in three octaves, each with cells and a life half its predecessor's, carried downwind.

gustAlong.description: The largest cells along the wind, in m.

gustAcross.description: The largest cells across the wind, in m.

gustLife.description: The largest cells' life, in s.

gustSpeed.description: How fast the field travels, as a share of a spell's wind at mid-disk.

gustVeer.description: How far the strongest gust veers, and the deepest lull backs by half, in degrees.

change.description: How long one spell takes to give way to the next, in minutes.

WeatherRing.title: WeatherRing
WeatherRing.description: The beginners' ring round gusts heading for the boat.

threshold.description: A patch gets a ring when its gust factor is this far from 1 toward the spell's.

spacing.description: The grid the field is sampled on upwind of the boat, in m.

depth.description: How far upwind the grid reaches, in m.

width.description: How wide the grid is across the wind, in m.

reach.description: A patch's track must pass this close to the boat, in m.

rate.description: Samplings of the field a second.

WeatherWaveWind.title: WeatherWaveWind
WeatherWaveWind.description: The wind that raises the waves: an exponential average of the mean wind at each sea area's centre.

waveTimeConstant.description: The average's time constant, in s.

waveSample.description: The wind is sampled on a grid of world time this far apart, in s: a whole number of seconds.

Regime.title: Regime
Regime.description: A kind of spell of weather.

share.description: The regime's share of the world's time.

frontal.description: A spell of it arrives and leaves as a front does: the wind veers.

next.description: The regimes a spell of it may give way to, by id.

RegimeWind.title: RegimeWind
RegimeWind.description: A regime's wind, from which each spell's is drawn.

speed.description: The least and the most of its wind at mid-disk, in knots.

gustFactor.description: Its strongest gusts as a multiple of the mean wind.

shift.description: How far its two oscillating shifts swing together, in degrees each way.

period.description: The shortest and the longest period of a shift, in minutes.

across.description: How far the wind's direction differs from the centre to the rim, in degrees.

drift.description: The most its direction moves over a spell, in degrees.

Sequence.title: Sequence
Sequence.description: The spells of weather until the world's weather is generated: this sequence, over and over from the world's epoch.

seed.description: The seed each spell's numbers are drawn with.

veer.description: How far the wind veers as a spell of a frontal regime arrives or leaves, the least and the most, in degrees.

swing.description: How far the wind's direction may move either way from one spell to the next otherwise, in degrees.

hours.description: How long it lasts, in whole hours.

Encounters.title: Encounters
Encounters.description: Boats meeting: their hulls touching, the wind one takes from another, and the Articles, the right-of-way rules that judge them.

EncountersContact.title: EncountersContact
EncountersContact.description: Two hulls touching: an impulse with no damage.

restitution.description: The share of the closing speed the hulls part with.

friction.description: Coulomb's coefficient of the hulls sliding along each other.

passes.description: Passes of the impulses over a tick's contacts.

push.description: The share of the rest of the penetration pushed apart in a tick.

cap.description: The most a contact pushes boats apart in a tick, in m.

apart.description: Ticks two boats must be apart before touching again is a new bump.

EncountersShadow.title: EncountersShadow
EncountersShadow.description: The wind shadow: the wake a sail leaves along its apparent wind, in units of its rig's height h above the water.

deficit.description: A: the share of the wind lost on the wake's axis one rig height behind.

near.description: s₀: closer than this, in h, the loss is no greater.

width.description: w: the wake's half-width parameter at one rig height, in h.

header.description: H: how far the wake turns the wind one rig height behind, in degrees.

deflection.description: How far the wake turns from the apparent wind toward the source's windward side: close-hauled, and on a reach and beyond, in degrees.

deflectionAt.description: The apparent wind angles at which each deflection holds, between which it blends, in degrees.

reach.description: How far the wake reaches, in h.

taper.description: Where it begins to fade to nothing at its reach, in h.

sources.description: The most wakes a boat feels at once: the nearest.

EncountersArticles.title: EncountersArticles
EncountersArticles.description: The numbers the Articles are computed with.

room.description: A boat that acquires right of way, or changes course, must give room for this long, in s.

turn.description: A change of course is one of more than this, in degrees.

course.description: The time constant of a boat's course: its heading, smoothed, in s.

pairs.description: Boats closer than this many hull lengths are remembered as a pair.

headToWind.description: Within this of head to wind a boat keeps the tack she had, in degrees.

EncountersOverlay.title: EncountersOverlay
EncountersOverlay.description: The beginners' right-of-way overlay, and dirty air drawn in the wind overlay.

range.description: Boats within this are considered, in m.

ahead.description: How far ahead their present motions are followed, in s.

close.description: A boat is marked when it comes within this many hull lengths.

marks.description: The most boats marked at once.

wedges.description: Dirty air is drawn behind boats within this, in m.

wedgeDeficit.description: Out to where the wind's loss falls under this share.

Sky.title: Sky
Sky.description: The sky's numbers: the lengths of its day, year and month, its scale, the moment it is counted from, and the stars with names. Where each body stands follows from these and the time alone.

day.description: The day, sunrise to sunrise, in minutes.

year.description: The year, in days: the stars gain one turn on the sun in it.

month.description: The moon's month, new moon to new moon, in days.

scale.description: Degrees of the sky to a nautical mile on the water: a boat that many miles nearer a star's point sees it one degree higher.

epoch.description: Sky time zero, in seconds of UTC since 1970: the same in every world.

sunAtEpoch.description: The sun's angle past noon at the centre of the disk, at the epoch, in degrees.

starsAtEpoch.description: The stars' turn beyond the sun's at the epoch, in degrees.

moonAtEpoch.description: The moon's age at the epoch, in degrees past new.

stars.description: The stars with names, the brightest of the navigator's.

NamedStar.title: NamedStar
NamedStar.description: A star with a name, at its place in the Bright Star Catalogue (J2000).

number.description: Its number in the Bright Star Catalogue (HR).

declination.description: Declination, in degrees. 90 is the pole itself, which the stars turn about.

Light.title: Light
Light.description: A navigation light a boat shows from sunset to sunrise, by the arc it shows over (International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea, Rule 21): a red sidelight to port and a green to starboard, each from right ahead to 22.5° abaft the beam; a white sternlight over the 135° astern; or the three combined in one lantern at the masthead, which Rule 25(b) allows a sailing vessel of less than 20 m.

Id.description: Stable identifier of a kind, stored in the database: never renamed or reused.

ArtPath.description: Path of an art file, relative to the repository's art/ folder.

BoatArt.title: BoatArt
BoatArt.description: A boat's art. Every art object's values are paths under art/, checked to exist.

model.description: The boat's model: a glTF binary with the nodes hull, mast, boom, sail, telltales, pennant, rudder, tiller, daggerboard and sailor, and a node for each of the boat's lights, named as the light, where its lantern is.

far.description: The boat's far model, drawn for boats seen from afar among many: the model's nodes but telltales, pennant and lights, with few segments.

model.description: The sailor's model: a glTF binary with the nodes body, head, arm-left and arm-right, its origin at the hips, facing +x.

far.description: The sailor's far model, drawn in boats seen from afar: the model's nodes, with few segments.

description.description: What the boat is, in a few words.

capacity.description: Most people aboard, the skipper included.

beam.description: Greatest width of the hull, in metres.

lights.description: The navigation lights the boat shows by night. Together their arcs make the full circle once.

BoatPhysics.title: BoatPhysics
BoatPhysics.description: The boat's physics, in SI units with angles in degrees. Every value is required.

PhysicsHull.title: PhysicsHull
PhysicsHull.description: The hull: its mass, resistance, inertia and stability.

displacement.description: Boat, rig and sailor, in kg.

waterlineLength.description: Length on the waterline, in m.

hullDraught.description: The hull's own draught, foils aside, in m.

centreOfGravity.description: Height of the centre of gravity above the waterline, in m.

dragAreaStep.description: Speed between entries of dragArea, in m/s.

dragArea.description: Upright resistance as a drag area (C_D A), at speeds 0, 1, 2 … times dragAreaStep, in m². Beyond the last, the last.

crossFlowDrag.description: Drag coefficient of the hull moving sideways, on waterline length times draught.

addedMassSurge.description: Added mass moving ahead, in kg.

addedMassSway.description: Added mass moving sideways, hull and foils, in kg.

munk.description: The hull's added mass sideways less its added mass ahead, for the Munk moment, in kg.

yawInertia.description: Moment of inertia in yaw, added inertia included, in kg·m².

rollInertia.description: Moment of inertia in roll, added inertia included, in kg·m².

rollDamping.description: The hull's own roll damping, in N·m·s/rad. The foils and sails damp through their flow.

rightingLever.description: Righting lever (GZ) with the sailor on the centreline, every 10° of heel from 0° to 180°, in m.

waterlineBeam.description: Beam on the waterline, in m.

waterplaneArea.description: Area of the waterplane, in m²: the heave stiffness is the water's weight per metre of it.

waterplanePitch.description: The waterplane's second moment of area about its transverse axis, in m⁴: the pitch stiffness.

addedMassHeave.description: Added mass moving up and down, in kg.

pitchInertia.description: Moment of inertia in pitch, added inertia included, in kg·m².

heaveDamping.description: Damping of the heave, as a fraction of critical.

pitchDamping.description: Damping of the pitch, as a fraction of critical.

waveForce.description: The share of the Froude–Krylov force of a wave's slope that pushes the hull along and across.

waveYaw.description: The share of that force's moment along the hull, which yaws the boat with the water of an oblique wave.

outline.description: The hull's half-beam at the sheer at 11 stations equally spaced from the transom to the stem, in m: its plan, where hulls touch. Convex, with the stem a point.

transom.description: The transom's distance aft of the centre of gravity, in m.

stem.description: The stem's distance forward of the centre of gravity, in m.

luff.description: Length of the luff, in m.

foot.description: Length of the foot, in m.

boomHeight.description: Height of the boom above the waterline, in m.

mastPosition.description: Distance of the mast ahead of the centre of gravity, in m.

footStrip.description: Height of the lower sail strip's centre of effort above the boom, as a fraction of the luff.

headStrip.description: Height of the upper sail strip's centre of effort above the boom, as a fraction of the luff.

pressureAttached.description: Centre of pressure aft of the mast with the flow attached, as a fraction of the foot.

pressureSeparated.description: Centre of pressure aft of the mast with the flow separated, as a fraction of the foot.

effectiveHeight.description: Effective rig height for induced drag, in m.

quadraticDrag.description: Drag growing with the square of the lift coefficient (k_pm).

maxLift.description: Greatest lift coefficient of the sail.

stallAngle.description: Angle of attack of the greatest lift, in degrees.

stallWidth.description: Angle past the stall over which the flow separates, in degrees.

sailDrag.description: Viscous drag coefficient of the sail.

luffAngle.description: Below this angle of attack the cloth flogs, in degrees.

flogDrag.description: Extra drag coefficient of flogging cloth.

normalForce.description: Normal force coefficient of separated flow over the sail, every 10° of angle of attack from 0° to 180°.

twistPowered.description: The upper strip's twist beyond the boom at full power, in degrees.

twistDepowered.description: The upper strip's twist at the flattest, in degrees.

twistEased.description: Extra twist with the boom let fly, growing in proportion to the boom's angle, in degrees. On a dinghy whose sheet also holds the boom down, easing it lets the leech open.

twistTurn.description: Boom angle over which the twist turns from one side to the other, in degrees.

headBacked.description: The upper sail strip's angle of attack at which the wind starts to get behind its leech, in degrees. A backed head swings across and its leech drags the boom over: an accidental gybe.

headBackedWidth.description: Angle of attack over which a backed head comes to drag the boom across, in degrees.

boomIn.description: The boom's angle off the centreline with the sheet hauled in hard, in degrees.

boomOut.description: The boom's angle with the sheet let fly, in degrees.

boomInertia.description: Moment of inertia of boom and sail about the mast, in kg·m².

boomMoment.description: Mass of boom and sail times the distance of their centre of gravity aft of the mast, in kg·m.

boomDamping.description: Friction of the boom about the mast, in N·m·s/rad.

windageFront.description: Drag area of hull, crew and spars from ahead, in m².

windageSide.description: Drag area of hull, crew and spars from abeam, in m².

windageHeight.description: Height of the windage's centre above the waterline, in m.

sailFloat.description: Upward force per metre a sail strip is pushed under the water, in N/m.

sailWaterDamping.description: Vertical damping of a sail strip in the water, in N·s/m.

closeHauled.description: The boat's close-hauled course: its heading off the true wind sailing as close to it as it sails well, in degrees.

PhysicsFoils.title: PhysicsFoils
PhysicsFoils.description: The daggerboard or keel, and the rudder.

boardSpan.description: Span of the daggerboard below the hull, in m.

boardChord.description: Chord of the daggerboard, in m.

boardPosition.description: Distance of the daggerboard ahead of the centre of gravity, in m.

rudderSpan.description: Span of the rudder below the hull, in m.

rudderChord.description: Chord of the rudder, in m.

rudderPosition.description: Distance of the rudder aft of the centre of gravity, in m.

foilStall.description: Angle of attack at which the foils stall, in degrees.

foilStallWidth.description: Angle past the stall over which their flow separates, in degrees.

foilDrag.description: Viscous drag coefficient of the foils, on plan area.

plateNormal.description: Normal force coefficient of a stalled foil.

pressureDepth.description: Depth of each foil's centre of pressure below the hull, as a fraction of its span.

carryOver.description: The hull's carry-over of the board's lift: k in 1 + k × hull draught / board span.

heelLoss.description: The board's lift lost per radian of heel.

rudderInflow.description: The rudder's share of the boat's speed through the water.

downwash.description: Share of the sideways flow from leeway that the daggerboard's downwash cancels at the rudder.

foilWetHeel.description: Heel up to which the foils are fully in the water, in degrees.

foilDryHeel.description: Heel from which the foils are out of the water, in degrees.

PhysicsSailor.title: PhysicsSailor
PhysicsSailor.description: What the sailor does by themselves: hiking, flattening the sail, righting the boat. The same for every player.

sailorMass.description: Mass of the sailor, in kg.

sailorSeatHeight.description: Height of the seated sailor's centre of gravity above the boat's, in m.

hikeReach.description: Furthest the sailor's centre of gravity goes out to windward, in m.

leeReach.description: Furthest it goes to leeward, in m.

hikeSpeed.description: Fastest the sailor moves across, in m/s.

hikeLag.description: The sailor's lag in moving, in s.

heelGain.description: Extra hiking per radian of heel, in m/rad.

rollRateGain.description: Extra hiking per rad/s of roll rate, in m·s/rad.

flattenFrom.description: Apparent wind at which the sailor starts flattening the sail, in m/s.

flattenTo.description: Apparent wind at which the sail is at its flattest, in m/s.

flattenMin.description: Flattest sail, as a fraction of full lift.

fallOutHeel.description: Heel past which the sailor falls in, in degrees.

climbInHeel.description: Heel below which the sailor climbs back in, in degrees.

boardReach.description: Distance of the sailor's weight on the daggerboard from the centre of gravity, in m.

sailorDrag.description: Roll damping of the sailor in the water, holding on to the boat, in N·m·s/rad.

swimTime.description: Time to swim to the daggerboard after falling in, in s.

climbTime.description: Time to climb back in, in s.

PhysicsRates.title: PhysicsRates
PhysicsRates.description: How fast the sailor's hands move the rudder and the sheet.

rudderTime.description: Time for the rudder's full travel, one side to the other, in s.

sheetHaulTime.description: Time to haul the sheet in over its full range, in s.

sheetEaseTime.description: Time to ease the sheet out over its full range, in s.

PhysicsAutopilot.title: PhysicsAutopilot
PhysicsAutopilot.description: How the boat's autopilot steers it: a proportional–integral–derivative law on the angle off its course, and how hard it turns in a tack or a gybe. It sets the helm only, at the sailor's rate.

gain.description: Helm per radian off course, the helm running from −1 to 1.

damping.description: Helm per rad/s of turn, against it: the counter rudder.

trimTime.description: Time for the standing helm to take up a steady error, in s: gain over this is its growth per radian-second.

trimLimit.description: The most standing helm, as a share of the helm.

trimBand.description: The standing helm grows only this near the course, in degrees.

tackHelm.description: The most helm in a tack.

gybeHelm.description: The most helm in a gybe.

byTheLee.description: How far by the lee the boat sails before the autopilot counts it gybed, in degrees. Below the angle at which the boom goes over by itself, about 17° on a dinghy.

onCourse.description: A tack or gybe ends this near its target, in degrees.

World.title: World
World.description: How a world is made from its seed, and how a boat meets its ground.

sizes.description: Size classes by an island's width, narrowest first.

land.description: The lowest and the highest land, in m.

talus.description: The angle of repose: ground steeper than this is cliff, in degrees.

biomes.description: The biomes: each an island's terrain.

surfaces.description: What the ground is covered with; a hexagon holds a surface's index here.

radius.description: The edge of the world from its centre, in m.

mist.description: Where the mist band begins, in nautical miles from the centre.

WorldZones.title: WorldZones
WorldZones.description: Where on the disk a place is: the centre, the middle waters and, beyond them, the rim.

centre.description: The centre reaches this far from the disk's centre, in nautical miles.

middle.description: The middle waters reach this far, in nautical miles.

WorldMainPort.title: WorldMainPort
WorldMainPort.description: The main port's island, at the centre of every world.

name.description: Its name, never drawn for another place.

across.description: Its width, the least and the most, in m.

height.description: Its highest point, the least and the most, in m.

cliffs.description: The share of its coast with cliffs.

offset.description: Its centre lies within this of the disk's, in m.

calm.description: No other land but its own rocks lies within this of the centre, in nautical miles.

rocks.description: Stacks off its coast, the least and the most.

WorldLayout.title: WorldLayout
WorldLayout.description: Where the islands lie and how big they are.

landmarkAcross.description: A landmark's width, the least and the most, in m.

landmarkApart.description: The least distance between two landmarks' centres, in m.

landmarkRing.description: Landmarks lie between these distances from the centre, in nautical miles.

korcak.description: Korčák's exponent b: the number of islands larger than an area a falls as a^−b.

islandRing.description: They lie between these distances from the centre, in nautical miles.

gap.description: The least gap between two islands' coasts, in m.

candidates.description: Candidate places tried for each island; the furthest from the land already placed is taken.

groups.description: Groups of rocks and islets, the fewest and the most.

groupSize.description: Rocks and islets in a group, the fewest and the most.

groupSpread.description: A group's rocks lie within this of its centre, in m.

WorldSize.title: WorldSize
WorldSize.description: A size class: the islands narrower than below and no narrower than the class before's.

class.description: The class's word, as the names give it.

below.description: The width it holds islands narrower than, in m.

WorldSeabed.title: WorldSeabed
WorldSeabed.description: The sea bed out from a coast: Dean's equilibrium profile to the closure depth, then the shelf, then the deep.

shelf.description: Beyond it the bed falls 1 m in this many.

deep.description: The deepest the bed is stored, in m.

reachBase.description: An island's bed reaches this far from its coast, in m, and more for a larger island.

reachPerRadius.description: Plus this many of the island's radius.

reachMost.description: At most this far, in m.

reachVaries.description: The share by which its reach varies along the coast.

flat.description: The flat behind it, in m deep.

offshore.description: The crest's distance from the coast, in m.

fore.description: The fore reef falls to this depth, in m.

passes.description: The share of the crest open as passes.

WorldErosion.title: WorldErosion
WorldErosion.description: Erosion on each island: thermal weathering, and droplets of rain.

dropletSteps.description: The most steps a droplet takes.

erode.description: Ground a droplet takes per metre it falls, in m.

deposit.description: The share of its load a droplet drops where it stops falling.

BiomeZones.title: BiomeZones
BiomeZones.description: A biome's weight in each zone.

BiomeSurfaces.title: BiomeSurfaces
BiomeSurfaces.description: The surfaces a biome's island is covered with.

height.description: Its highest point, the least and the most, in m.

lobes.description: The lobes its shape is made of, the fewest and the most.

elongation.description: A lobe's length over its width.

warp.description: How far its shape is warped, as a share of its radius.

bays.description: Bays bitten into its coast, the fewest and the most.

rise.description: The exponent its height rises by with the distance inland.

hills.description: The share of rolling hills in its height.

crater.description: The chance of a crater in the cone.

cliffs.description: The share of its coast with cliffs.

beach.description: The width of low ground along its other shores, in m.

dean.description: Dean's A of its sea bed, in m^(1/3).

stacks.description: Stacks off its coast, the fewest and the most.

split.description: The height, as a share of its highest, above which its high surface lies.

Surface.title: Surface
Surface.description: What the ground is covered with.

friction.description: Coulomb's coefficient of a hull dragging on it under water.

WorldFetch.title: WorldFetch
WorldFetch.description: Each sea area's effective fetch for a wind from each of 16 directions.

step.description: A radial's step upwind, in m.

WorldShelter.title: WorldShelter
WorldShelter.description: The land's shelter for the wind.

reach.description: How far upwind land is looked for, in m.

near.description: In the lee closer than this many heights the wind is at its least.

far.description: Beyond this many it is whole again.

least.description: The least factor on the wind's speed.

speedUp.description: The most land beside the wind's path speeds it, as a share.

flank.description: Land beside the path speeds it within this many heights of it.

turn.description: The most land on one side turns the wind, in degrees.

offsets.description: How far beside the path land is looked for, in m.

WorldStart.title: WorldStart
WorldStart.description: Where boats start: the stretch of water off the main port with the most room.

within.description: The start area begins within this of the coast, in m.

depth.description: A place has at least this much water, in m.

clear.description: And no land within this, in m.

spacing.description: Places are this far apart, in m.

stillSpeed.description: Slower than this a boat aground is still, in m/s.

stillTime.description: Still this long, its sailor pushes it off, in s.

pushDepth.description: Into water this deep, in m.

restitution.description: The share of its closing speed a hull parts from land with.

friction.description: Coulomb's coefficient of a hull sliding along land.

WorldValidator.title: WorldValidator
WorldValidator.description: The rules a world must pass.

centreOffset.description: The main port's centre from the disk's, at most, in m.

landShare.description: Land as a percentage of the disk, the least and the most.

counts.description: Each size class within this share of its expected count.

openWater.description: Inside the mist band no water is further than this from land, in m.

shoreline.description: A landmark's shoreline development index, at least.

reachDepth.description: Every landmark reachable from the start in this much water, in m.

NameFeature.title: NameFeature
NameFeature.description: A feature a name may need, by its word, and what shows it: 0 or false for a test it does not have; a feature with none is never shown.

word.description: Its word, as the names give it.

cliffs.description: A coast with at least this share of cliff.

peak.description: A summit at least this high, in m.

twin.description: Two summits each at least this share of the highest.

twinApart.description: And at least this far apart, in m.

lagoon.description: A lagoon behind a reef at least this wide, in m.

NameTone.title: NameTone
NameTone.description: A tone of names: its weight in each zone, and how many a world may have.

word.description: Its word, as the names give it.

most.description: The most names of it in a world; 0 for no limit.

phantom.description: Its names that belong only to the rim are given only in the mist band.

neighbours.description: Two islands of a biome this close may share a name, in m.

prefixes.description: The pairs of words neighbours sharing a name take, the larger the first: two words each.

calf.description: An islet this close to a larger island may be named after it, in m.

partners.description: Names written as a pair, best given in the same world: two names each.
